processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Sample heated to 1200 °C at a rate of 10 °C/s (common preheat for the compression schedule).
Homogenized by holding for 120 s at 1200 °C.
Cooled from 1200 °C to the set deformation temperature (1000 °C for this sample) at 5 °C/s.
Held 15 s at the set temperature (1000 °C) before compression so that the temperature difference between the inside and outside of the sample is the same.

Compressed at 1000 °C at a constant strain rate of 0.1 s⁻¹ to a maximum compression of 60% (true strain 0.92). Mica foils with high-temperature lubricants were affixed to the two end faces to reduce friction and deformation non-uniformity. Cylindrical sample Ø8 mm × 12 mm.
After compression the sample was sprayed with water to cool it down; figure_002 annotates 'Quenching'.

structures.overall_structure: Initial (pre-deformation) microstructure of the forging billet: large polygonal grains delimited by bright, continuous, slightly etched boundaries enclosing dark grey grain interiors. Within essentially every grain the interior carries many fine, closely spaced, parallel light-grey striations/lamellae whose direction changes from grain to grain, giving a strongly banded, dendritic/interdendritic segregation contrast rather than a uniform solid solution; a few grains appear almost featureless while others are densely striped, indicating chemical heterogeneity in the as-forged condition.

grain_structure.grain_size_distribution: Large polygonal grains; individual grains span roughly one to a few times the 100 µm scale bar length

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Sample split in half along the axial axis; after preparation, grinding, polishing and etching with 30% nitric acid alcohol solution (volume fraction); 100 µm scale bar.
characterization_methods.purpose: Observe the initial microstructure and the hot-deformed (DRX) microstructure in the three deformation zones of the compressed sample.
characterization_methods.key_findings: Initial microstructure consists of large polygonal grains with bright etched boundaries and abundant fine parallel light striations (segregation banding); as-forged condition is chemically heterogeneous.

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Temperatures 900-1150 °C, strain rates 0.01-10 s⁻¹, maximum compression 60% (true strain 0.92); this sample at 1000 °C and 0.1 s⁻¹.
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure rheological (flow) stress curves and study dynamic recrystallization behavior of the Fe-Mn-Al-C steel.
characterization_methods.key_findings: The steel is a negative temperature-sensitive and positive strain-rate-sensitive material; flow stress decreases with decreasing strain rate or increasing temperature.

computational_details.simulation_method: Constitutive analysis: Zener-Hollomon parameter calculation (temperature-compensated strain rate)

analytical_models.equation_role: Characterize the combined influence of temperature and strain rate on the rheological stress
analytical_models.model_note: lnZ value for this sample (T = 1000 °C, ε̇ = 0.1 s⁻¹) taken from Table 1; Qp is the activation energy for dynamic recrystallization of the steel.

unmapped_findings: For this sample (T = 1000 °C, ε̇ = 0.1 s⁻¹) the Zener-Hollomon parameter is lnZ = 60.99 (Table 1).

This sample's deformation condition (1000 °C, 0.1 s⁻¹) lies within the processing window 950-1000 °C / 0.01-0.1 s⁻¹ that the paper identifies as producing a relatively fine and uniform dynamically recrystallized grain structure.

The paper states that with increasing Z parameter (i.e. increasing strain rate or decreasing temperature) the initiation and completion of dynamic recrystallization become more difficult; lnZ decreases with increasing temperature within a strain-rate row and increases with increasing strain rate within a temperature column.

No explicit peak stress, characteristic strain/stress values or measured DRX average grain size specific to the 1000 °C / 0.1 s⁻¹ condition are individually reported in the text; such values are given only through general models/figures (Eq. 10, Fig. 6, Fig. 10) applicable across all conditions.
